decision: Audit against WCAG 2.2 AA. Plan: record URL/component, OS, browser, screen reader, viewport, zoom and date. Open checkout using the keyboard; inspect initial focus, Tab/Shift+Tab containment, visible and unobscured focus, activation, close behavior and focus restoration. Inspect dialog role, accessible name and background inertness in the accessibility tree. Submit empty and invalid values; check error identification, field associations, invalid states and timely screen reader announcements. Test normal size, 200% text resize and 400% zoom/reflow. Supplement manual testing with a scanner. Finding A11Y-01: reported modal focus remains behind the overlay, potentially blocking keyboard checkout; provisional high severity, needs human check. Investigate WCAG 2.4.3 and 2.1.1 against reproduced behavior. Finding A11Y-02: reported validation error is not announced; needs human check, with severity based on whether recovery is blocked. Investigate 3.3.1, 3.3.3, 1.3.1 and, where the message qualifies as a status message, 4.1.3. Missing speech alone does not establish every listed failure.
verification: Only local guidance was inspected; no application, screenshot, code or assistive technology testing was performed. Capture repeatable steps, expected versus actual behavior and evidence before marking findings verified. Acceptance: opening places focus appropriately inside the modal; keyboard navigation stays within it while open; closing restores focus appropriately; errors are identified, associated and discoverable through an appropriate announcement or focus strategy without duplicate speech. Recheck valid, invalid, async and nested states. Report tested browser/AT combinations and untested criteria. A screenshot cannot establish WCAG 2.2 AA conformance.
safety: All actions were read-only. No network, production, database, deployment or destructive actions occurred. Next, reproduce the reported issues in an authorized test environment using test checkout data, without completing a purchase.
